Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

  8
 STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  SUBJECT:  PROPOSED USE OF THE STATE  OF CALIFORNIA  2026/27 CANNABIS
  TAX FUND GRANT PROGRAM  (CTFGP)

  PURPOSE: To approve the use of Cannabis Tax Fund GrantProgram  ("CTF Grant") funds inthe
  amount of $98,790 for overtime, equipnnent, and training.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a. Aulhorizing utilization  of  the 2026-2027 CTF Grant funds in the amount of $98,790 for
  overtime, training  and equipment;
  b. Amending  the Fiscal Year 2026/27 Law Enforcement Grants Fund Budget by
  appropriating $23,040 for overtime salaries, $10,000 for taining  and $65,750 for
  equipment, specifically  a  new  police motorcycle;  and
  c. Authorizing the Cmef of Police or his designee to execute the CTF Grant Agreement in a
  form acceptable to the City Attorney,

  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no fiscal impact to the General Fund, and no requirement for the
  City to provide matching funds. The total amount of funding that has been allocatedto the City for
  FY 2026/27 is $98,790. The funds must increase or enhance the City's existing programs and may
  not be used to replace funding the City would otherwise provide,

  ANALYSIS:  The South Gate Police Department submitted a grant application to the California
  Highway Patrol ("CHP") Cannabis Tax Fund Gtant Programin early 2026, In June 2026, the CHP
  awarded the Department $98,790 for overtime to cover impaired-driving enforcement operations,
  personnel training and education, as well as approved equipment directly conriected to impaired-
  driving enforcement.

  BACKGROUND:  With the passage of Proposition 64, the Control, Regulate, and Tax Adult Use
  of Marijuana Act ("AUMA"),  Califoria  voters mandated the State set aside funding for the CHP
  to award grants to local governments and qualified nonprofit organizations, as described in
  Revenue and Taxation Code Section 34019(f)(3)(B),

  The CTF Grant marks an important step toward reducing impaired driving crashes, increasing
  public awareness surrounding the dangers of impaired driving, and making California's roadways

  11
 a safer place  to travel.

The  CHP  works  closely  with  state  and  local  agencies  and  other  traffic  safety  stakeholders  to
actively  address  impaired  driving.  The  CHP  will  consider  a variety  of factors  in determining
specific  needs  for each grant  cycle,  including  opportunities  and projects  best suited  to prevent  the
loss of life,  injuries,  and property  damage  caused  by driving  under  the influence  of alcohol  and/or
drugs.

The funding  provided  is appropriated  by the California  State Controller's  Office,  and all grants  are
awarded  on a competitive  basis,  unless  otherwise  specified  within  the Request  for  Application.
The CHP  may  consider  an extended  project  performance  period  based  on need,  as determined  by
the CHP.  The awarding  of a grant  does not guarantee  ongoing  or future  funding.

Project  Description
SGPD has seen a steady rise in collisions caused by intoxicated drivers. This is according to statistical data
involving alcohol and drugs since the legalization of marijuana. The SGPD impaired driving enforcement
project strategy consists of three points: Training, Education, and enforcement.  SGPD will promote public
awareness of the dangers of DUI/DLIID. Enforcement of D.U.I. laws pertaining to DUI/DUID and associated
collision factors will reduce the number of citizens killed or injured in collisions.

We will enhance public safety and aim to reduce the number of persons killed or injured in collisions involving
alcohol, drugs, and marijuana. SGPD will distribute informative safety material to drivers of all ages about the
effects of alcohol, drugs, and marijuana on driving. We will utilize social media and community presentations
to heighten awareness. Project funds will be used for D.U.I. saturation patrol overtime salaries and a
dedicated D.U.I. enforcement vehicles to carry out enforcement efforts. SGPD will also provide police officers
the needed training to recognize the signs and symptoms of impairment. Funds will be used to train additional
police officers to recognize the signs and symptoms of impairment for DUI investigations.  Community
outreach can be accomplished  through social media outreach to highlight awareness and purchase
equipment to support our DUI enforcement and prosecution efforts. During this time police officers will gain
proper training and experience in identifying drivers under the influence of alcohol, drugs, and marijuana. By
accomplishing  this we are able to better serve our communities as we improve public safety.

Problem Statement
The South Gate Police Department is facing a significant public safety crisis stemming from an increase  in
impaired driving incidents and the abuse of cannabis within the community. The South Gate Police
Department has seen an overall increase in the number DUI related collisions dating back to 2020.

2020-(68  DUI/DUID  related collisions  and 3 fatal collisions  with 1 being DUI/DUID  related)

2021-(100  DUI/DUID  related collisions  and 8 fatal collisions  with one being DUI/DUID  related)

2022-(94  DUI/DUID  related collisions  and 4 fatal collisions  with no DUI/DUID  collisions  being reported)

2023- (138 DUI/DUID  related collisions  and 7 fatal collisions  with 2 of them being DUI/DUID  related fatalities)

2024-(80  DLII/DUID  related collisions  and 5 fatal collisions  with 3 of them being DUI/DUID  related fatalities)

2025-(126  DUI related collisions  and 7 fatal collisions  with 4 of them being DUI/DLIID  related fatalities)

This has shown a steady increase in DUI/DUID related collisions and the dangers the community faces.
Further, with the data provided by the Office of traffic safety for the 2023 and 2022 calendar year, the City of
South Gate ranks 9th (2023) and 1 5th (2022) out of 103 California cities. Both years show that South Gate
falls in the top tier of California cities for DUI/DLIID related collisions per person. A combination of education
and enforcement is critical to protect the members of this community. In previous years staffing shortages
made it difficult to field DLII enforcement patrols, however, with staffing levels at 75 (Full staffing at 81). While
this has not entirely eliminated mandatory assigned patrol overtime, it has drastically decreased the number
of officers forced to work patrol overtime freeing up resources to deploy locally for enforcement.

In addition, the community is grappling with a rise in cannabis abuse, particularly among juveniles. SGPD has
made multiple arrests related to the illegal sale of cannabis vape pens near middle and high schools.
These investigations  have uncovered links to other criminal activities, such as possession of stolen vehicles
and weapons. The increased use of cannabis products among juveniles has resulted in unsafe behaviors,
including impaired operation of bicycles, e-bikes, scooters, skateboards,  pocket bikes, and vehicles,
further endangering public safety.

This multifaceted issue highlights the urgent need for community education, enhanced officer training, and
increased enforcement efforts to address impaired driving and cannabis abuse. Without strategic intervention,
the safety of SGPD's community will continue to be at risk.

Performance  Measures/Scope  of Work (Proposed  Solution)
The South Gate Police Department's  Impaired Driving Enforcement Grant aims to save lives and ensure the
long-term benefits of its efforts. By increasing public awareness and implementing targeted enforcement, the
SGPD seeks to achieve a 10% reduction in both DUI-related incidents and fatal collisions.

To achieve this goal, the SGPD will conduct 28 DUI enforcement operations throughout the grant year with 7
per quarter (every three months). These operations will focus on identifying and apprehending  impaired
drivers to reduce injuries and fatalities. Officers involved in these operations will utilize specialized training,
including Standardized  Field Sobriety Test (SFST) and Advanced Roadside Impaired Driving Enforcement
(ARIDE) techniques, to conduct thorough DUI/DUID investigations.

Overtime salaries will support these operations, with each detail involving a single vehicle staffed by one
officer to increase coverage and visibility. These enforcement efforts will primarily occur during nighttime
hours or other high-risk periods for impaired driving, with each operation lasting eight hours. The goal is to
conduct seven enforcement operations per quarter throughout the grant period.

A dedicated marked "DUI Enforcement" vehicle will facilitate these efforts in addition to marked police
motorcycles. These vehicle will allow officers to effectively locate and apprehend impaired drivers while
addressing key collision factors such as speeding, unsafe turning movements, and failure to yield. By
providing officers with the tools necessary for targeted enforcement, the vehicle and motorcycles will enhance
the department's  ability to reduce DUI-related incidents and fatalities while reinforcing its commitment to
community safety.

To accomplish this, the SGPD intends to conduct a total of 28 DLII saturation patrols (Q1 =7, Q2=7, Q3=7,
Q4=7)  and aim to reduce DUI/DUID deaths and DUI/DUID related crashes by IO%.

Project Performance  Evaluation
The South Gate Police Department will analyze data collected during the grant to complete a final evaluation
in the fourth quarter. This evaluation will summarize the grants accomplishments,  challenges and key
activities. It will also include an assessment of whether the goals of the objective were met, exceeded, or, if
not achieved, an explanation why. SGPD will use Crossroads Analytics Software and in-house RMS software
to track collision and enforcement data. This data will allow for comparisons  between the grant year and
previous years, helping to identify trends and assess the grant's potential impact. Statistics on DUI arrests,
DUI-related traffic collisions, injury-related DUI collisions, and DUI traffic fatalities will also be compiled for
quarterly evaluations.

Program  Sustainability
The South Gate Police Department  is committed  to reducing reliance on future grant funding by building
sustainable  enforcement  and prevention  capabilities  within its traffic division. As staffing levels improve, the
department's  long-term  plan is to fully staff the traffic division with four motor officers, two DUI enforcement
vehicles, and eight community  service officers. A fully staffed traffic division will enable SGPD to conduct
consistent  and proactive DUI enforcement  efforts without the need for external funding.  With these resources
in place, the traffic division will be able to focus on targeted enforcement  strategies  such as saturation  patrols,
sobriety checkpoints,  and community  outreach programs, ensuring continued efforts to reduce DUI-related
incidents and fatalities. Additionally,  community  service  officers will play a crucial role in supporting  non-
enforcement  duties, allowing sworn officers to dedicate  more time to DUI enforcement.  The timeline for
achieving this objective is directly tied to improvements  in staffing levels. As recruitment  and retention
strategies take effect, the SGPD anticipates  incremental  progress over the next three to five years. During this
period, the department  will prioritize internal  training for officers, ensuring they are equipped with the skills
necessary  to maintain and expand DUI enforcement  efforts independently  of grant funding. This transition  plan
emphasizes  self-sufficiency while maintaining  a focus on roadway safety, ensuring the community  continues  to
benefit from effective DUI enforcement  and prevention  measures  even in the absence of significant  grant
support.

Administrative  Support
The South Gate Police Department  has extensive  experience  successfully managing various grants, even
amidst challenges  such as a reduction in police personnel.  The department  has consistently maintained
accurate record-keeping,  data entry, and statistical reporting to ensure the success of its grant-funded
projects. SGPD has efficiently handled the processing  of all financial records and will continue to manage and
retain records for the Office of Traffic Safety, Alcohol Beverage Control and any other entity we enter into an
agreement  with. With a dedicated  and motivated  staff, the South Gate PD is well-prepared  to undertake  the
tasks necessary  to reduce DUI incidents and enhance public safety within the community.  The department's
personnel  and physical resources are well-suited  to implement  the project effectively and achieve its
objectives.

ANALYSIS:  On June 9, 2026, the City Council  adopted  the amended  and restated  resolution  and
ordinance  placing  the Measure  before  the voters  at the rate of 8 percent.  On July 14, 2026,  at the
request  of members  of the City  Council,  staff  presented  an analysis  of whether  a sunset  clause
should  be added,  addressing  the duration  of the City's  structural  deficit,  the fiscal  effect  of a
scheduled  expiration  of  the  revenue,  potential  borrowing  and  credit  considerations,  and  the
practice  of other  Los Angeles  County  jurisdictions.  Following  that discussion,  the City  Council
provided  direction  to leave  the Measure  unchanged  and to return  with  a resolution  outlining  a
future  review  of the city's  finances  and the UUT.

What  the Resolution  Provides

  1.  Five-Year  Fiscal  Review.  The City  Council  will  conduct  a comprehensive  public  review
  of the City's  finances  during  the fifth  full fiscal year of {JUT  collections;  a partial  fiscal  year
  in which  collections  first commence  does not count  as a full  fiscal  year. The review  will  be
  presented  at a noticed  public  meeting  no later than April  30, 2032,  so the City  Council  has
  time  to deliberate  and, if it chooses,  to act before  applicable  election  deadlines.  Based  on
  the anticipated  commencement  of collections,  the review  is expected  to occur  during  Fiscal
  Year 2031-32.

  2.  Minimum  Review  Elements.  The  review  will  include,  at a minimum:  UUT  revenues
  collected  compared  to projections;  the condition  of the General  Fund,  including  structural
  balance,  reserve  levels  measured  against  the City's  adopted  reserve  policies,  and the five-
  year forecast;  the status of General  Fund services  restored,  sustained,  or enhanced  following
  implementation  of the Measure,  including  the  service  priorities  identified  in the  City's
  adopted  budgets  and public  financial  reports;  and whether  the UUT  rate remains  appropriate
  to the City's  financial  condition  and service  needs.  The review  will  be based  on audited
  results  through  the most recently  completed  fiscal  year and current-year  estimates.

  3.  Consideration  of Future  Action.  As part  of the review,  the City  Council  will  consider
  whether  the UUT  rate should  remain  unchanged,  be reduced  pursuant  to any  authority
  provided  by the UUT  ordinance,  or be submitted  to the voters  for adjustment  or repeal,  as
  required  by law.  The UUT  ordinance  authorizes  the City  Council  to amend  the ordinance
  without  an election  except  for amendments  that would  increase  the tax within  the meaning
  of Governrnent  Code  section  53750(h);  any increase  above  the voter-approved  maximum
  would  require  voter  approval  under  Article  XIII  C of the California  Constitution.

  4.  Public  Process.  The  staff  report  and supporting  analysis  will  be published  on the City's
  website  in advance  of the meeting,  and members  of the public  will  have the opportunity  to
  comment.

  5.  Annual  Reporting.  In addition  to the five-year  review,  the Director  of Administrative
  Services,  or designee,  will  report  aru'iually  on UUT  collections  and the condition  of the
  General  Fund through  the budget  process  and the City's  audited  financial  statements.

  6.  General  Tax  Status.  Nothing  in the resolution  restricts  UUT  proceeds  to a specific  purpose
  or changes  the  Measure's  status  as a general  tax  available  for  general  governmental
  purposes.

  under  Article  XIII  C of the California  Constitution  to reduce  or repeal  a local  tax  by

  8.  Effective  and Operative  Dates.  The resolution  is effective  upon adoption;  its reporting  and

  become  operative.

Relationship  to the Ballot  Measure
The  proposed  resolution  implements  the  City  Council's  July  14  direction  by  establishing  a
scheduled  public  fiscal  review  without  changing  the rate,  duration,  or other  provisions  of the
Measure  already  approved  for the ballot.  The review  will  provide  the City  Council  and the public
with  updated  financial  information  and a formal  opportunity  to consider  whether  further  action  is
warranted.

Procedural  Considerations
Adoption  of the resolution  does not amend the UUT  ordinance,  ballot  question,  tax rate, or duration
of the Measure  previously  approved  for the November  3, 2026 ballot.  The resolution  will  become
effective  upon adoption,  but the annual  reporting  and Five-Year  Fiscal  Review  requirements  will
become  operative  only  upon  certification  of election  results  confirming  voter  approval  of the
Measure.

Nature  of the Commitment
The resolution  establishes  a formal  policy  and administrative  direction  that will  remain  in effect
unless amended  or repealed  by a future  City  Council  in open session.  It does not predetermine  the
outcome  of the review  or require  the placement  of a fiiture  ballot  measure.  Its purpose  is to
establish  a scheduled,  transparent  process  for  evaluating  the City's  financial  condition  and the
continued  appropriateness  of the UUT  rate.

BACKGROUND:  The Active  Transportation  Program  (ATP)  Cycle  8 Grant Funding  Program  provided
the City  with  an opportunity  to pursue  competitive  funding  for pedestrian,  bicycle,  transit  access,  and
multimodal  connectivity  improvements.  In March  2026,  the City  solicited  proposals  from  qualified

Corridor  Connectivity  Project  and the Southern  Avenue  Multimodal  Bridge  Project.  Following  a Request
for  Proposals  (RFP)  process,  the City  administratively  awarded  Contract  No.  2026-28-AC  to HDR
Engineering,  Inc, to provide  professional  grant application  support  services,  in the amount  of $39,874.

The  proposed  Atlantic  Avenue  Corridor  Connectivity  Project  included  improvements  intended  to
strengthen  connectivity  along Atlantic  Avenue  and nearby  corridors,  including  improved  access to South
Gate Park, future  transit  service,  Wright  Road median  improvements,  and evaluation  of Southern  Avenue
from  Pinehurst  Street to the Los Angeles  River.

The proposed  Southern  Avenue  Multimodal  Bridge  Project  builds  upon  a previously  submitted  ATP
grant  application  and advances  plans  for a new multimodal  bridge  along  Southern  Avenue  that would
accommodate  pedestrians,  bicyclists,  and transit  users.  The  project  would  create  a new  connection
between  Atlantic  Avenue  and  Garfield  Avenue  over  the  Los  Angeles  River  and  I-710  Freeway,

SUBJECT:  AGfflEMENT  WITH  GENERAL  PUMP  COMPANY,  INC.,  FOR  ON-CALL
MAINTENANCE  SERVICES  FOR  THE  MUNICIPAL  WATER  SYSTEM

PURPOSF,:  To award  an on-call  maintenance  services  agreement  to General  Pump  Company,  Inc,
to provide specialized emergency well maintenance  and repair services  for the City's  municipal  water
system on an as-needed basis using competitively bid unit prices.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:

  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  General  Pump Company,  Inc., to perform  well maintenance
  services on an as-needed basis ("Agreement"),  for a three-year  term with two optional  one-
  year extensions,  in an annual amount  not to exceed $100,000  for a total of $300,00o  for the
  initial three-year  term; and

  b.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to the  City
  Attorney,

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact  to 'the General  Fund. The Agreement  has a total not-to-exceed
amount of $300,000  over the initial  three-year  term. The Agreement  will  be funded  by the Water Fund,
with $100,000  budgeted  annually  in the Public  Works  Operating  Budget,  subject  to annual  budget
appropriations,

ANALYSIS:  The  City  owns  and operates  a municipal  water  system  that  includes  eight  active
groundwater  wells  used to supply  drinking  water  to the community.  These  wells  contain  complex
mechanical  and  electrical  equipment,  including  motors,  pumps,  electrical  control  panels,  and
associated  piping,  all of which  require  periodic  maintenance  and occasional  emergency  tepairs.  When
critical  components  fail,  repairs  must often  be completed  on an expedited  basis to maintain  reliable
water production  and avoid potential  interiuptions  in water service.

While  City  staff perform  routine  maintenance  whenever  practical,  certain  repairs  require  specialized
equipment,  technical  expertise,  and certified  maintenance  contractors,  For these situations,  the Public
Works  Department  maintains  the  ability  to  quickly  secure  the  services  of  a qualified  specialty
contractor  to perform  emergency  repairs and specialized  maintenance.

Staff  is recomrnend'ing  awarding  an on-call  maintenance  services  agreement  to  General  Pump
Company,  Inc. to provide  these specialized  services  on an as-needed  basis. The Agreement  establishes
competitively  bid  init  prices  and enables  the City  to respond  quickly  to emergency  well  failures
without  the delays associated  with  procuring  a separate  contract  for each repair,  This  approach  helps

  1

  113
 maintain  the reliability  of the City's  water  system,  minimizes  downtime,  and ensures  the continued
delivery  of safe and dependable  drinking  water  to the community.

BACKGROUND:  The  City  owns  and operates  a municipal  water  system  that  provides  drinking
water  service  to more  than  14,250  water  service  accounts,  serving  approximately  90 percent  of the
City's  residents  and businesses.  The municipal  water  system  consists  of more than 135 miles  of water
mains,  eight  active  groundwater  wells,  four  reservoir  sites,  and multiple  booster  pump  stations  that
work  together  to provide  a safe, reliable,  and unintermpted  water  supply  throughout  the community.

The City's  groundwater  wells  extract  water  from  underground  aquifers  and serve as the primary  source
of  the  City's  drinking  water.  Each  is well  equipped  with  specialized  mechanical  and  electrical
equipment,  including  pumps,  motors,  electrical  control  panels,  well  casings,  and associated  piping.
Like  all mechanical  infrastructure,  these  components  are subject  to normal  wear,  deterioration,  and
unexpected  failures  that require  routine  maintenance  and, at times,  emergency  repairs  to help maintain
continuous  water  production.  While  City  staff  perform  routine  maintenance  whenever  practical,
certain  repairs  require  specialized  equipment,  technical  expertise,  and  certified  maintenance
contractors.  These  services  include  pump  removal  and  installation,  motor  replacement,  electrical
control  repairs,  well  casing  inspections,  well  cleaning  and  rehabilitation,  flow  testing,  and  other
specialized  maintenance  activities  that caru'iot be efficiently  or safely  performed  by City  personnel.

To ensure  these specialized  services  are readily  available  when  needed,  the City  publicly  advertised  a
Notice  Inviting  Bids  on June 4, 2026,  through  PlanetBids  and in a newspaper  of general  circulation.
On  July  1, 2026,  the  City  received  two  responsive  bids  from  General  Pump  Company,  Inc.  and
Bakersfield  Well  & Pump  Company,  which  were publicly  opened  by the City  Clerk.

Staff  conducted  a comprehensive  evaluation  by comparing  the submitted  unit prices  for all anticipated
work  items.  General  Pump  submitted  the  lowest  overall  pricing,  with  an  evaluated  total  of
approximately  $37,367,  compared  to  $108,301  submitted  by  Bakersfield  Well  &  Pump  Company,
representing  an  overall  cost  savings  of  approximately  65.5  percent.  The  greatest  savings  were
associated  with  the  work  items  most  frequently  utilized  during  emergency  well  maintenance  and
rehabilitation  projects,  including  mobilization,  pump  removal  and installation,  discharge  compliance,
and well  redevelopment  services.  Based  on the bid  evaluation,  staff  determined  that  General  Pump
Company,  Inc. submitted  the lowest  responsive  and responsible  bid and provides  the best overall  value
to the City.

General  Pump  Company,  Inc. has successfully  provided  well  maintenance  services  to the City  of South
Gate  since  2009,  consistently  delivering  quality  workmanship,  timely  emergency  response,  and
dependable  service.  Based  on this proven  performance,  the firm  has established  a strong  track  record
of supporting  the City's  municipal  water  system.  Headquartered  in San Dimas,  California,  General
Pump  Company,  Inc. has specialized  in municipal  well  maintenance  services  since 1952  and employs
more than 50 personnel.  In addition  to South  Gate, the company  currently  provides  similar  services  to
numerous  public  agencies  throughout  Southern  California,  including  the  Cities  of  Ontario,  Santa
Monica,  Lynwood,  Compton,  Chino,  and Redlands.

Based  on  the  firm's  qualifications,  competitive  pricing,  and  demonstrated  performance,  staff
recommends  awarding  the Agreement  to General  Pump  Company,  Inc.

  Purpose

  The  purpose  of this program  is to ensure  the safety  of all employees  and contractors  working  for  General  Pump
  Company,  Inc. and to comply  with  all regulations  and host clients  that  pertain  to confined  spaces.

  Scope

  This program  covers  all employees  and other  workers  that may be involved  in confined  space entry.  When  work  is
  performed  on a non-owned  or operated  site, the operator's  program  shall take precedence.  This document  covers
  General  Pump  Company,  Inc.  employees  and contractors  and  shall  be  used  on owned  premises,  or when  an
  operator's  program  doesn't  exist or is less stringent.

  Definitions

  Attendant  - an individual  stationed  outside  one  or more  Confined  spaces  who  monitors  the authorized  Entrants
  and who  performs  all Attendant's  duties  assigned  in the  General  Pump  Company,  Inc. Confined  Spaces  Program.
  Attendants  must have sufficiently  completed  and fully  understands  the Confined  Space training  and is approved  by
  the HSE Manager  to work  in a confined  space as an Attendant.

  Authorized  Entrant  - an individual  who  is authorized  by General  Pump  Company,  Inc. to enter  a confined  space.
  Entrants  must  have  sufficiently  completed  and fully  understands  the Confined  Space training  and is approved  by
  the HSE Manager  to work  in a confined  space as an Authorized  Entrant.

  Confined  Space

  A space  that is large  enough  and so configured  that an employee  can bodily  enter  and perform  assigned
  work;
  Has limited  or  restricted  means  for  entry  or exit  (for  example,  tanks,  vessels,  coolers,  storage  bins,
  hoppers,  vaults,  and pits are spaces that may have limited  means  of entry);  a nd
  Is not designed  for continuous  occupancy.

  Confined  Space Entry Permit  - A confined  space entry  permit  must be completed  before  entering  a confined  space.
  An  entry  permit  is the  written  or printed  document  that controls  entry  into  a confined  space.  Before  entry  is
  authorized,  an entry  permit  documenting  control  measures  to protect  workers  from  the hazards  in the confined
  space  must  be  prepared.  Procedures  necessary  for  concluding  the  entry  after  entry  operations  have  been
  completed  must  be in place.  When  workers  from  multiple  employers  are working  in a permit  space,  procedures
  must  be implemented  to ensure  workers  from  one employer  do not endanger  workers  of another.

  Entry  - the action  by which  a person  passes through  an opening  into a confined  space.  Entry includes  ensuing  work
  activities  in that  space  and  is considered  to have  occurred  as soon  as any part of the Entrant's  body  breaks  the
  plane of an opening  into the space.

  Entry  Supervisor  - the person  responsible  for determining  if acceptable  entry  conditions  are present  at a confined
  space where  entry  is planned,  for authorizing  entry  and overseeing  entry  operations,  and for terminating  entry  as
  required  by this section.

  Entry Supervisors  must have sufficiently  completed  and fully understands  the Confined  Space training  and
  is approved  by the HSE Manager  to work  in a confined  space.
  An Entry Supervisor  also may serve  as an Attendant  or as an authorized  Entrant,  as long as that  person  is
  trained  and equipped  as required  by this section  for  each  role  he or she fills. Also, the duties  of Entry
  Supervisor  may be passed from  one individual  to another  during  the course  of an entry  operation.
  The Entry Supervisor  is responsible  to test and monitor  the atmosphere  conditions.

  Hazardous  atmosphere  - an atmosphere  that  may  expose  employees  to the  risk of death,  incapacitation,  and
  impairment  of ability  to self-rescue  (that  is, escape  unaided from a confined space), irJury, or acute illness from
  one or more  of the following  causes:

  Flammable  gas, vapor,  or mist in excess of 10 percent  of its lower  flammable  limit  (LFL), (0% is normal).
  Atmospheric  oxygen  concentration  below 19.5  percent  or above  23.5 percent,  (20.9 % is normal).
  Any  other  atmospheric  condition  that  is immediately  dangerous  to  life  or health.  (Ex.-H2S 10%,  0% is
  normal).
  Note:  For air contaminants  for  which  OSHA  has not  determined  a dose  or permissible  exposure  limit,
  other  sources  of  information,  such  as Safety  Data Sheets  that  comply  with  the  Hazard  Communication
  Standard,  published  information,  and internal  documents  can provide  guidance  in establishing  acceptable
  atmospheric  conditions.

  Immediately  dangerous  to life or health  (I[)LH)  - any condition  that poses  an immediate  or delayed  threat  to life or
  that  would  cause  irreversible  adverse  health  effects  or that would  interfere  with  an individual's  ability  to escape
  unaided  from  a confined  space.

  Note:  Some  materials-hydrogen  fluoride  gas  and  cadmium  vapor,  for  example-may  produce
  immediate  transient  effects  that,  even  if severe,  may pass without  medical  attention,  but are followed  by
  sudden,  possibly  fatal collapse  12-72  hours  after  exposure.  The victim  "feels  normal"  from  recovery  from
  transient  effects  until  collapse.  Such materials  in hazardous  quantities  are considered  to be "immediately
  dangerous  to life or health".

  Inerting  - the  displacement  of the  atmosphere  in a permit  space  by a non-combustible  gas (such  as nitrogen)  to
  such  an  extent  that  the  resulting  atmosphere  is non-combustible.  This  procedure  produces  an IDLH oxygen
  deficient  atmosphere.

  Non-Permit  Confined  Space - A confined  space that does not contain  or, with respect  to atmospheric  hazards,  have
  the potential  to contain  any hazard  capable  of causing  death  or serious  physical  harm.

  Oxygen  deficient  atmosphere  - an atmosphere  containing  less than 19.5  percent  oxygen  by volume.

  Oxygen  enriched  atmosphere  - an atmosphere  containing  more  than  23.5 percent  oxygen  by volume.

  Permit-Required  Confined  Space - a confined  space that  has one or more  of the following  characteristics:

  Contains  or has a potential  to contain  a hazardous  atmosphere.
  Contains  a material  that has the potential  for engulfing  an Entrant.

  Responsibilities

  Managers/Supervisor
  *  Shall ensure  that all employees  have been trained  and fully u nderstand  the requirements  of this program.
  Shall provide  the  necessary  equipment  to comply  with  these  requirements  and ensure  that all employees
  are trained  on its use.
  Shall ensure  that all confined  space assessments  have been conducted  and documented.
  Shall ensure  that all Permit-Required  Confined  Spaces permits  are posted.
  Shall ensure  an annual  review  of the  program  including  all entry  permits  issued that during  that  annual
  period.
  Shall  ensure  that  all confined  spaces  that  have  been  identified  as "no  entry"  have  signs  that  state,
  "DANGER-  DO NOT ENTER".
  Shall ensure  signs have  been  posted  at all Permit-Required  Confined  Space areas that state, "DANGER  -
  PERMIT  ENTRY  CONFINED  SPACE"  along  with  the  proper  warning  word  such  as "ASPHYXIANT,
  FLAMMABILITY  or TOXIC HAZARD"
  Shall file all permits  at the area offices  for review.  Permits  shall  be kept on file for one year.

  Affected  Employee
  *  Shall attend  Confined  Space  Entry  training  commensurate  with  their  duties  and  when  duties  change  as
  required.
  Shall comply  with  all aspects  of this program.
  Authorized  Entrants,  Attendants  and  Entry  Supervisors  may  be  any  General  Pump  Company,  Inc.
  employee  that  is authorized  by management  to work  in a confined  space  setting  and that  has been
  trained  and is proficientin  the understanding  of program  requirements.

  Duties  of Entrants,  Attendants  and  Entry  Supervisors

  All affected  employees  must understand  the hazards  of going into  a confined  space.

  Attendants  are the workers  who watch  the entrance  to the confined  space. They communicate  with  the entrants
  and know  how many entrants  are in the confined  space.  They also ask for  help  in an emergency  and do not enter
  the confined  space.

  Entrants,  the  workers  who  go into  the  confined  space,  must  know  how  to use equipment  and communicate  with
  the attendant  to check-in  or ask for rescue.

  Entry  supervisors  check  the  atmospheric  monitoring  being  done  and make sure all hazards  have been  identified
  and mitigated.  They also make sure  help  is available  if a rescue  is needed  and keep  the area free  of unauthorized
  people.

  Pre-Job  Planning  and Space  Preparation

  TM Entry Supervisor  must  determine  that  the  confined  space  is properly  isolated  by blinding,  disconnecting,
  and/or  by following  local  Lockout/Tagout  procedures.

  The  Entry  Supervisor  must  discuss  with  all  Entrants  the  hazards  of  the  space,  communication  methods  and
  emergency  procedures  during  the confined  space entry.

  Eliminate  any condition  making  it unsafe to open the equipment  to atmosphere.

  Promptly  guard  the  opening  to  prevent  an accidental  fall through  the  opening  and to protect  each  employee
  working  in the space from  foreign  objects  entering  the space.

  If applicable,  wash, steam,  ventilate  or degas the confined  space  to properly  free  it of possible  contaminants.  Vent
  vapors  to a safe location.

  Do not allow unauthorized personnel to enter a confined space. Barricade and/or guard all confined spaces to
  prevent  entry  of unauthorized  Entrants.

  If performing  hot  work  in the  confined  space,  precautions  must  be taken  consistent  with  the  General  Pump
  Company,  Inc. Hot Work  Permit  procedure.

  Ensure  that vehicle  or other  equipment  exhaust  does not enter  the space.

  Pre-EntrySafety  Meeting
  The Entry  Supervisor  must declare  when the confined  space is ready  for entry.

  The  Entry  Supervisor  shall  hold  a pre-entry  safety  meeting  to discuss  all requirements  and procedures  with  all
  authorized  Entrant(s)  and  Attendant(s)  involved  with  the  entry.  He/she  will  discuss  other  concerns  such  as
  previous  contents,  vessel  coating,  PPE required  etc., during  this meeting.

  The  Entry  Supervisor  must coordinate  entry  operations  when  employees  of more  than one company  are working
  simultaneously  in the  confined  space.  This  coordination  is necessary  so that  one  company's  work  does  not
  endanger  the employees  of another  company.

  Equipment
  Check  all work  equipment  to ensure  that it has the proper  safety  features  and is approved  for the locations  where
  it will be used.  The Entry  Supervisor  shall ensure  that all equipment  is properly  maintained  in a safe condition  and
  that  Entrants  use the equipment  properly.

  The following  equipment  must  be considered  and may be required  when  entering  a confined  space:

  Atmospheric  Testing  and  Monitoring  Equipment.
  Use of Barriers  or Barricades  -  Measures  necessary  to prevent  unauthorized  entry  must  be implemented.
  Pedestrian,  vehicle  and  other  barriers  necessary  to  protect  entrants  from  external  hazards  must  be
  provided.

  Post  signs  outside  all Permit-Required  Confined  Spaces  to notify  personnel  that  a confined  space  entry  is
  in  progress  and  unauthorized  entry  is prohibited.  Any  signs  used  must  state  "Danger  -  Permit  Entry
  Confined  Space"  along  with  the  proper  warning  word  such  as "Asphyxiant,  Flammability  or Toxic  Hazard".
  Communications  Equipment  -  Only  use  intrinsically  safe  equipment  in  areas  where  a  hazardous

  atmosphere  may  exist.  Use  a communication  system  that  will  keep  the  Attendant  in  constant,  direct
  communication  with  the  Entrant(s)  working  in the  confined  space.  Also,  use  a communication  system
  that  allows  the Attendant  to summon  help  from  rescue  or emergency  service.
  Entry  and Exit Equipment  - (For  example:  ladders  may  be needed  for  safe entry  and exit).
  Lighting  Equipment  -  Needed  for  safe  entry,  work  within  the  space  and  exit.  Lighting  equipment  used  in
  the  confined  space  must  be certified  safe for  the  location.

  Portable  electric lighting used in wet and/or  other  conductive  locations  (drums,  tanks, vessels) must be
  operated  at 12 volts  or less. 120  volt  lights  may  be used  if protected  by a ground-fault  circuit  interrupter.
  Personal  Protective  Equipment  - Ensure  that  personnel  wear  the  required  personal  protective  equipment.
  For respiratory  protection  requirements,  refer  to the  Respiratory  Protection  Program.
  Rescue  and Emergency  Equipment  - Except  if provided  by outside  rescue  services.
  The Attendants  must  also  have  an approved  first  aid  kit.
  Vacuum  Trucks  - When  used,  trucks  must  be properly  grounded  or bonded  to prevent  static  sparks.
  Ventilating  Equipment  -  Local  exhaust  air  movers  used  to obtain  acceptable  atmospheric  entry  conditions
  (e.g.,  Copus  air movers).
  Other  -  Any  other  equipment  necessary  for  safe  entry  into  and  rescue  from  permit  required  confined
  spaces.

  @  Before  an employee  enters  the  space,  the  internal  atmosphere  shall  be tested,  with  a calibrated  direct-
  reading  instrument,  for  oxygen  content,  for  flammable  gases  and  vapors,  and  for  potential  toxic  air
  contaminants,  in that  order.  The  atmosphere  within  the  space  must  be periodically  tested  as necessary  to
  ensure  that  the  continuous  forced  air  ventilation  is  preventing  the  accumulation  of  a  hazardous
  atmosphere.
  Entrants  are informed  of atmospheric  testing  results.

  Employees  or their  representatives  are entitled  to request  additional  air monitoring  at any time.

  Ventilation

  Continuous  forced  air ventilation  must  be cised and tested  as follows:

  An  employee  may  not  enter  the  space  until  the  forced  air  ventilation  has  eliminated  any  hazardous
  atmosphere;
  The  forced  air ventilation  shall  be so directed  as to ventilate  the  immediate  areas  where  an employee  is or

  will  be present  within  the  space  and  shall  continue  until  all employees  have  left  the  space;

  Means  of Communication  Used to Summon  Rescue

  Procedures  for  summoning  rescue  and  emergency  services  must  be developed  and implemented  to perform
  rescue,  to provide  necessary  emergency  services  to rescued  employees,  and to prevent  unauthorized  personnel

  Below  are our procedures.

  (B;3H1

  Non-entry  Rescue

  To facilitate  non-entry  rescue,  an Entrant  must be attached  to a retrieval  system whenever  he/she  enters
  a Permit-Required  Confined  Space with  a vertical  depth  of more  than  5 feet.
  The  retrieval  equipment  is not  required  if it will  increase  the  overall  risk of the entry,  e.g., creating  an
  entanglement  hazard,  or will not contribute  to the rescue  of the Entrant.
  Each  Entrant  shall  use a full  body  harness  equipped  with  a "D"  ring  located  between  the  shoulders  or
  above  the head.
  Wristlets  may be used instead  of the full body harness,  if the use of the full body harness  is not feasible  or
  creates  a greater  hazard  and that using wristlets  is the safest  and most  effective  alternative.
  The  retrieval  line  must  be attached  to the "D"  ring and the other  end of the retrieval  line  attached  to a
  retrieval  device  or fixed  point  located  outside  the space so that  rescue  can begin  as soon as the rescuer
  becomes  aware that  rescue  is necessary.

  Issuance/Reviewing  of Permit
  Only  when  all pre-entry  requirements  are  satisfied,  the  Entry  Supervisor  shall  issue  a completed  and  signed
  confined  space permit.  The confined  space  permit  is valid for one shift.

  An annual  review  of this program,  using  the  cancelled  permits  retained  within  1 year  after  each  entry  shall be
  conducted  by the  HSE Manager  to revise  the  program  as necessary,  to ensure  that employees  are protected.  If
  no confined  space entries  were  performed  during  a 12-month  period,  no review  is necessary.

  Terminating  and Closing  Out a Confined  Space Permit
  The  confined  space  permit  may  need  to  be terminated  in  some  situations,  such  as when  new  hazards  are
  introduced.  Procedures  for terminating  the permit  and closing  it out after  job completion  must  be included.

  The Entry  Supervisor  shall terminate  the confined  space  permit,  at the end of the job operation,  at the e nd of the
  shift or when  the  Entry Supervisor  or Attendant  determine  that  when  new hazards are introduced  or conditions  in
  or near the confined  space have changed  and is hazardous  to the Entrants.

  The  Entry  Supervisor  shall,  at the  conclusion  of entry  operation,  close  out  the  permit  and provide  the  safety
  department  the original  copy of the Confined  Space Permit.

  Training

  Employees  are provided  confined  space training.

  Each affected  employee  must  be trained  prior  to initial  assignment,  prior  to a change  in assigned  duties,  if a new
  hazard  has been  created  or special  deviations  have occurred.  Before  beginning  work  at a worksite,  General  Pump
  Company,  Inc. must  ensure  that  a competent  person  identifies  all confined  spaces  in which  one or more  of their
  employees  may work,  and identifies  each space that is a permit  space, through  consideration  and evaluation  of the
  elements  of that  space, including  testing  as necessary.

  Training  records  must be documented  and made available  to employees  and their  authorized  representative(s).

  The employee  shall be retrained:

  Whenever  there  is a change  in confined  space  operations  that  presents  a hazard  about  which  an
  employee  has not previously  been trained.
  Whenever  the  supervisor  has reason  to believe  either  that  there  are deviations  from  the permit  space
  entry  procedures  required  by this section  or thatthere  are inadequacies  in the employee's  knowledge  or
  use ofthese  procedures.

  The training  shall establish  employee  proficiency  in the duties  required  by this program  and shall introduce  new or
  revised  procedures,  as necessary.

  The supervisor  shall certify  that the training  required  by this program  has been accomplished.

  The certification  shall  contain  each  employee's  name,  the  signatures  or initials  of the trainers,  and the
  dates of training.
  The  certification  shall  be  available  for  inspection  by  employees,  their  authorized  representatives,
  management,  clients  and the safety  department.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council will consider:

  a. Approving a Professional Services Agreement ("Agreement") with Windan

  ANALYSIS:  The Public Works Department has a need for additional support associated with the
  vacancy of the Street and Sewer Superintendent position within the Field Operations Division.
  This vacancy has increased demands onexisting management staff and potentially risks impacting
  thedivision's capacityto efficiently coordinate daily maintenance operations, contractor oversight,
  and program implementation.

  To help maintain continuity of operations and ensure critical field activities continue without
  disruption, staff recommends utilizing professional program and contract management support
  services through Willdan Engineeririg. The proposed Agreement will provide part-time support to
  assist the Field Operations Division with operational coordination, program management, and
  contract  administration.

 Services  to be provided  iu'ider the Agreement  include  coordination  of maintenance  activities  and
operational  priorities;  contractor,  consultant,  and utility  coordination;  work  order  and  service
request  monitoring;  program  tracking;  contract  administration;  operational  reporting;  and support

existing  staff  resources  and improve  the division's  ability  to manage  ongoing  maintenance  and
infrastructure-related  activities.

The  Field  Operations  Division  is responsible  for  overseeing  critical  citywide  maintenance

numerous  maintenance,  service,  and infrastructure-related  contracts  that  support  essential  field
operations  throughout  the City.

These responsibilities  require  significant  day-to-day  operational  coordination,  including  contractor
oversight,  scheduling,  contract  administration,  program  tracking,  documentation,  and
interdepartmental  coordination  to ensure  services  are delivered  efficiently  and in accordance  with
City  standards  and operational  priorities.

The proposed  Agreement  will  allow  the Department  to continue  receiving  operational  support  and
contract  management  assistance  while  recruitment  for  the  Street  and  Sewer  Superintendent
position  remains  ongoing.  This  support  is necessary  to maintain  service  continuity,  operational
efficiency,  and uninterrupted  delivery  of critical  field  services.

Mr. Nandino's  Property is the subject of a marital  dissolution  proceeding  between Petitioner  Ana Dolores
Nandino  and Respondent  Ramon Nandino,  in which the City of South Gate has appeared as
Claimant/Intervenor.  Because the Property  is being transferred  by judicial  decree rather than in an arms-
length sale, the Note requires the fair market value to be established  by a qualified  appraisal.  An April  10,
2026 appraisal established a fair market value of $700,000. The parties have stipulated  to the $700,000
fair market value and that, should the community  residence be awarded to Petitioner,  Petitioner  will pay
the City $145,000.

ANALYSIS:  Applying  the Note's  formula,  the amount  payable  to the City  is calculated  as
follows:  the appraised  value  of $700,000,  less the original  value  of $179,500,  yields  appreciation
of $520,500;  less the City's  original  $40,000  principal  yields "Proceeds  of Sale"  of $480,000;
22% of which  is $105,600,  for a total payable  to the City  of $145,000  (return  of the $40,000
principal  plus the $105,600  appreciation  share).

To release the City's  lien upon payment,  the City Attorney  has prepared  a Substitution  of Trustee
and Deed of Full  Reconveyance  under  which  the City  substitutes  itself  as Trustee  in place of
Comprehensive  Housing  Services,  Inc. pursuant  to Section  24 of the Deed of Trust,  and, as
substituted  Trustee,  reconveys  the Property  without  warranty  to the person(s)  legally  entitled
thereto.  So that the City's  security  is not released  before  it is paid, the executed  and notarized
instrument  is to be delivered  to escrow  (with  instructions  not to record  or release  it until  the loan
proceeds  are deliverable  to the City)  or, if payment  is not handled  through  escrow,  held by the
City  Attorney  and recorded  only  after the City  receives  the fund.

  2

  194
 CONCLUSION:  Staff recommends adoption of the attached Resolution approving  the Substitution
of Trustee and Deed of Full Reconveyance and authorizing its execution and delivery upon the
conditions described above, so that the City's subordinate deed of 'hst lien is released only after the
City has received the $145,000 payoff owed under the Nandino shared appreciation loan.

  SUBJECT:  TO ACCEPT  A PRIVATE  DONATION  AND  RATIFY  THE  PURCHASE
  AND TRAIINING  OF A POLICE  CANINE  (K9).

  PURPOSE: To authorize the acceptance of a $20,000 private donation from Mr. Ronald Loynds
  to assist with the purchase and training of a Police Service Cariine (K9) for the South Gate Police
  Department,to ratify the purchaseand training alreaay initiated with Gold Coast K9 Servicesi
  LLCI,  and to amend the Fiscal Year 2026-2027  Budget accordingly

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a.  Accepting and ratifying receipt of a private donation in the amount of $20,000 from Mr,
  RonaId Loynds for the purchase and training of a K9 and recognizing the donation as
  revenue  in the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget;
  b.  Amending the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Budget by appropriating $20,000 for the purchase
  and training of a K9 (100-502-21-9005  ($8,500) and 100-502-21-6340  ($f 1,500)), funded
  by the $20,000 in donation revenue; and
  c.  Ratifyirig the purchase and training of the Police Service Canine from Gold Coast K9
  Services, LLC in the total amount of $20,871,25, as reflected in Invoice No. SGPD-38
  (Attachment A),

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no fiscal impact to the City's General Fund from the acquisition  of
  the canine.  The total cost for the purchase of the Police Service Canine is $8,500 (IOO-502-21-
  9005) and the cost of initial ti'aining is $11,500 (100-502-21-6340),  plus $871,25 for taxes (235-
  570-21-6340), for a total project cost of $20,871.25. The $20,000 donation from Mr. Ronald
  Loynds will offset aportion ofthese costs. The remaining balance ($871.25) is budgeted in the FY
  2026-27 Police Departtnent budget and funded through the Police Department's Asset Forfeiture
  Fund, The use of Asset Forfeiture Funds for canine acquisition is a permissible law enforcement
  expenditure under applicable state and federal asset forfeitute  guidelines, and these funds
  supplement, rather than supplant, existing appropriations.  Ongoing program costs, including
  veterinary care, food, equipment, and handler canine-care compensation required under the Fair
  Labor Standards Act, will continue to be absorbed within the K9 Program's existing operatirig
  budget, as the new canine replaces medically retired K9 Chavo on a one-for-one basis,

  ANALYSIS:  The South Gate Police  Depattnent  has maintained  a successful  Police  Canine

  227
 Program  that enhances  officer  safety,  assists in apprehending  suspects,  locates  missing  persons,
and supports  narcotics  enforcement  operations.  The Department  has previously  received  generous
donations  from  Mr.  Ronald  Loynds  that have funded  the purchase  and training  of Police  Service
Canines  currently  assigned  to the Department.

Mr.  Loynds  has once again  demonstrated  his commitment  to public  safety  by donating  $20,000
toward  the purchase  and training  of a replacement  patrol  K9.  Acceptance  of this donation  will
enable the Department  to continue  maintaining  a fully  operational  K9 Program  without  placing  an
additional  burden  on the City's  General  Fund.

BACKGROUND:  The  South  Gate Police  Department's  K9 Program  currently  consists  of two
Patrol  Service  Canines  and one Narcotics  Detection  Canine.  These K9s were acquired  through  the
generosity  of Mr.  Ronald  Loynds,  whose  continued  support  has been instrumental  in the success
of the program.

Approximately  two  months  ago, K9  Chavo  was medically  retired  due to health  complications,
creating  the need to replace  one of the Department's  patrol  service  dogs.

To ensure continuity  of the K9 Program,  Mr. Loynds  generously  donated  $20,000  for the purchase
and training  of a replacement  Police  Service  Canine.  The Department  has initiated  the purchase  of
the new K9 from  Gold  Coast K9 Services,  and the canine  is currently  undergoing  handler  training
with  Officer  Ocampo.  Due  to the  operational  need to restore  patrol  canine  coverage  and the
vendor's  scheduled  handler  school,  the purchase  was initiated  in advance  of Council  action;  the
recommended  actions,  therefore,  include  ratification  of the purchase.  Gold  Coast K9 Services  LLC
supplied  and  trained  the  Department's  existing  canines,  and  continuity  of  vendor,  canine
evaluation,  and training  methodology  supports  this selection  consistent  with  the City's  purchasing
procedures.  The donated  funds have been received  and deposited  by the City.  The team is expected
to successfully  complete  certification  and become  operational  on or about August  14, 2026.

The Police  Department  respectfully  requests  that the City  Council  accept this generous  donation,
ratify  the purchase,  and appropriate  the funds  to support  the acquisition  and training  of the new
Police  Service  Canine.

WATER  CONT'D  Mario  Dominguez,  a South  Gate resident,  asked whether  the City  has
  sufficient  water  available  to respond  to a major  fire disaster.

  Liz Ruiz,  a South  Gate resident,  asked where  the water  shortage
  contingency  plan could  be found  online.

  Having  no one else come forward,  Mayor  Barron  closed  the audience
  portion.

  Coiu'icilwoman  Avalos  asked how often the city is required  to submit  this
  report  to the state.

  Arturo  Cervantes,  Director  of Public  Works,  stated that the plan must be
  filed  every  five years, with  the current  filing  deadline  set for June 30.

  Mr. Chen explained  that the schedule  allows  water  agencies  and systems
  to collect  data through  2025 and incorporate  it into the plan.

  Councilwoman  Avalos  expressed  concern  that data centers  can place
  significant  strain on water  resources.  She asked whether  any nearby  data
  center development  could  affect  South  Gate residents  or the City's  water
  supply.

  Mr. Cervantes  is not aware  of any proposed  or active  data center
  development  projects  within  the city.

  Councilwoman  Avalos  clarified  that her concern  was not about data center
  development  within  South  Gate, but in neighboring  cities.  She asked
  whether  such development  could  affect  South  Gate residents  or the City's
  water  supply.

  Mr. Cervantes  asked Mr. Chen to explain  how groundwater  use by other
  agencies  could  affect  South  Gate's  groundwater  supply.

  Mr. Chen explained  that groundwater  rights  in the basin are adjudicated.
  Any  water  agency  that produces  groundwater  from  the Central  Basin  must
  stay within  its allotted  rights  unless  it leases additional  water  rights  from
  another  rights  holder.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated that the City holds  more than 11,000  acre-feet  of
  water rights  and uses approximately  8,300 acre-feet.  Regardless  of
  whether  other agencies  use their  own allocations,  South  Gate retains
  access to the groundwater  amount  authorized  under  its water  rights.

WATER  CONT'D  Vice Mayor  Rios acknowledged  that the City  has sufficient  water  supply
  but noted that residents  have been asked to conserve  water  in the past. He
  asked whether  all groundwater  wells  are located  within  South Gate or
  whether  some are shared with  neighboring  communities.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated that the City's  water  system  is fully  dependent  on

  groundwater.  Although  the City has access to imported  water,  such as
  water  from  the Metropolitan  Water District,  its sufficient  groundwater
  rights  allow  it to rely entirely  on groundwater  and avoid  drawing  water
  from  other sources.

  Vice  Mayor  Rios asked whether  the City's  groundwater  is free from
  contamination.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated that the City's  water  quality  is regulated  by the state
  and must meet standards  for numerous  groundwater  constituents.
  Although  groundwater  conditions  and constituent  levels  may vary, the
  City  tests its water regularly,  producing  more than 2,000 water  samples
  each year. He noted that the city has consistently  met state and federal
  water  quality  standards,  and the City's  water  is considered  safe for use.

  Mayor  Barron  asked whether  the question  about the water  shortage
  contingency  plan could  be addressed.

  Mr. Chen stated that the Water  Shortage  Contingency  Plan is included  in
  Chapter  8 of the Urban  Water Management  Plan.

  Mayor  Barron  asked whether  the Water  Shortage  Contingency  Plan had
  been updated.

  Mr. Castillo  stated that residents  can find the City's  master  planning
  documents  by searching  for master  reports.

  Mayor  Barron  asked whether  the City  has sufficient  water  available  to
  serve South  Gate residents  during  an emergency.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated that the city has a reliable  and robust  water  system,
